close_reason: Landed in e55c256. ClientError::Parse(serde_json::Error) and ClientError::Serialize(serde_json::Error) variants reshaped to opaque ParseError/SerializeError wrappers, matching the existing HttpError/WebSocketError isolation pattern. The wrappers expose line/column/classify accessors that return workspace-local types (ParseCategory enum, not serde_json::error::Category), so callers are insulated from a future JSON-parser swap. Construction path is ClientError::from_parse(serde_json::Error)/from_serialize — extension client crates migrated from .map_err(ClientError::Parse) to .map_err(ClientError::from_parse) via sed across ~100 call sites in 8 extension-client crates (chat, mail, calendars, tasks, contacts, sharing, filenode, metadata). 5 new unit tests in error.rs cover the new accessor surface.
description:
error.rs:249-250 — Parse(serde_json::Error)
error.rs:302-303 — Serialize(serde_json::Error)
error.rs:255-261 — BlobIntegrityMismatch { expected: String, actual: String }

The SemVer-isolation work (HttpError, WebSocketError, InvalidHeaderValueError wrappers) intentionally hides reqwest::Error and tungstenite::Error from the public surface. Excellent.

But ClientError::Parse(serde_json::Error) and ClientError::Serialize(serde_json::Error) directly expose serde_json::Error. If serde_json eventually goes to 2.0 (which is plausible — serde itself has been pre-1.0 forever for the same reason, but serde_json has had multiple discussions about a major bump), this crate's public API ships an unwrapped third-party error in a public variant.

The asymmetry is:
- reqwest:    wrapped via HttpError ✓
- tungstenite: wrapped via WebSocketError ✓
- reqwest::header::InvalidHeaderValue: wrapped via InvalidHeaderValueError ✓
- serde_json::Error: bare ✗

This pre-dates the SemVer-isolation work (the variant has always been bare); landing the wrapping today is a breaking change because callers matching on `ClientError::Parse(e) => e.line()` etc. would need to switch to a new wrapper-type accessor. But it's worth flagging now so the next major (perhaps the JMAP-6by7 typed-Id epic) can do all three asymmetric leaks at once.

The "construct explicitly: `.map_err(ClientError::Parse)`" pattern documented in error.rs:248 also commits the crate to letting external code construct Parse variants. A future wrapper would need to remain construction-compatible — or break that pattern (likely the latter).

Recommendation: file follow-up bead to wrap serde_json::Error behind a ParseError wrapper type with accessor methods (e.g., `line()`, `column()`, `classify()`) in the next major bump. Document the SemVer policy in the crate-level docs so it's clear that serde_json is currently a "leak" while reqwest is not.
title: ClientError::Parse and Serialize variants expose serde_json::Error as public payload — major-version lock on serde_json
